text: Three papers. (1) FASEB J 2001 (10.1096/fj.00-0815fje): cholesterol is essential for synaptic plasticity and neuronal degeneration; ex vivo cholesterol efflux induced by human CSF-HDL3 and methyl-β-cyclodextrin impairs short- and long-term plasticity in adult rat hippocampal slices (CA1 fEPSPs). (2) ATM deficiency causes nuclear HDAC4 accumulation in neurons, driving ataxia-telangiectasia neurodegeneration; nuclear HDAC4 binds chromatin, MEF2A and CREB, altering gene expression. Blocking HDAC4 activity or nuclear accumulation rescues ATM-deficient mouse behaviors, though full rescue requires cytoplasmic HDAC4; ATM phosphorylation downregulates PP2A, excess activity of which dephosphorylates HDAC4. (3) Osteoblast-secreted PGE2 activates sensory-nerve EP4, inhibiting sympathetic activity via the CNS to regulate bone formation; PGE2 rises as bone density falls in osteoporotic models, and sensory nerve ablation erodes skeletal integrity.
